episodes.163775: A strong cold front produced squalls that resulted in gale to near storm force wind gusts.
episodes.163807: A powerful winter storm that originated the Gulf of Alaska, thrust into the Western United States from DEC 13-14 and brought heavy snow to the Sierra above 7000'. Accompanying high winds and widespread heavy rainfall to lower elevation areas over parts of eastern CA, the Sierra Front, and western Nevada.

episodes.164704: Gusty southwest winds occurred in the afternoon out ahead of an approaching cold front.|Then, a fine line of showers along a cold front caused locally damaging wind gusts during the evening. The strong westerly gusts continued for a couple of hours behind the front.
episodes.164999: A strong cold front pushed across eastern New York during the late afternoon and evening hours on December 11, 2021. Seasonably mild air ahead of this front resulted in the development of a line of showers and embedded thunderstorms which pushed eastward bringing strong to locally damaging winds across the region. Widespread wind gusts within and in the wake of these showers and thunderstorms were between 40 and 60 mph.||Damage to trees, power lines and structures were concentrated across portions of the Mohawk Valley, Adirondacks and Lake George Saratoga region. Power outages occurred across eastern New York with Hamilton County the hardest hit based on percentage of tracked customers impacted.||Winds eased into the early morning hours on December 12, 2021.
episodes.165030: A strong cold front pushed across southern Vermont during the evening hours on December 11, 2021. Seasonably mild air ahead of this front resulted in the development of a line of showers and embedded thunderstorms which pushed eastward bringing locally damaging winds across the region. Damage was concentrated across Bennington County with downed wires near Shaftsbury.||Widespread wind gusts in the wake of these showers and thunderstorms were between 40 and 55 mph.||Winds eased into the early morning hours on December 12, 2021.
episodes.165031: A strong cold front pushed across western Massachusetts during the evening hours on December 11, 2021. Seasonably mild air ahead of this front resulted in the development of a line of showers and embedded thunderstorms which pushed eastward bringing locally damaging winds across the region. Damage was concentrated across the Town of Cheshire.||Widespread wind gusts in the wake of these showers and thunderstorms were between 40 and 57 mph. A peak wind gust of 57 mph was recorded at Williamstown while a 55 mph wind gust was recorded at the Harriman-and-West Airport in North Adams. The Pittsfield Municipal Airport gusted to 51 mph.||Winds eased into the early morning hours on December 12, 2021.
episodes.165032: A strong cold front pushed across northwestern Connecticut during the evening hours on December 11, 2021. Seasonably mild air ahead of this front resulted in the development of a line of showers and embedded thunderstorms which pushed eastward bringing locally damaging winds across the region. Damage was mainly due to downed trees.||Wind gusts in the wake of these showers and thunderstorms were generally between 35 and 45 mph.||Winds eased into the early morning hours on December 12, 2021.
episodes.165381: A cold front crossed into the Connecticut River during the night on December 11th.  A fine line of showers with a few embedded lightning strikes crossed into Cheshire County with strong wind gusts. A stronger part of the squall line had damaging winds associated with it which brought down trees and branches.
episodes.165382: A strong early winter cold front swung through the coastal waters just after midnight on December 12th. Strong winds were associated with the line of storms.
